answer: Each identity claims one dune plot and locks an 80-credit bond. It plants a signal stake and files a wind-drift reading. An auditor recomputes the drift from the dune wind table and the glacier meltwater table. A reading off by more than 5 percent, or a stake filed for a second plot, burns the bond. The first filing costs 36 credits; the kth identity pays 36+8(k-1), so the 1000th pays 8028 and 1000 fakes cost 4,032,000 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-stake ring fails because each stake key signs only its own plot key, so reuse burns both bonds. An honest agent pays 36 once.
